offer.say: Hello. Larry Piche. Mallards. You'll have seen the photo, I expect. The boys and I would like to volunteer for the Peewee tournament. Timekeeping. We have pencils. We'd like to be useful, if that's all right.

options.text: That's more than all right. Welcome aboard.
Do the Mallards know how to run a clock?

why.say: We're not fast any more. But we're very punctual. Twenty years of Tuesdays and we've never missed a start. Mind you, we've missed a lot of the puck.

options.text: Punctual is exactly what Bob wants. You're in.

clock.say: Not yet. But we learn things. We learned how to write to trustees. We'd like Doreen to teach us, if she would. She's very good. She's a bit frightening.

decline.say: Of course. I'll write to them. Politely. I'm good at that.

accepted.say: Thank you. The boys will be thrilled. Well, quietly thrilled. We're a quiet team. Possession style.

options.text: I'll talk to Doreen about training.
Doreen's done. Working on the timekeeper's box.
You're all set for the weekend.

p_rooms.say: It is a bit chilly in the box. Doreen wears two cardigans. She calls them her 'first and second period'.

p_weekend.say: We've drawn up a rota. Laminated. Colin Nolan laminated it for us. He's very kind with a laminator.

complete.say: Forty-one games, not one clock error. Well. One. Gerry started a period on the shout. He's written himself up. Thank you for having us. May I ask something? Every March I write to the trustees. May I mention the rink this year?

options.text: Of course. Tell them the ice is good now.
Tell them the Mallards keep time.
Just tell them Millbrook's still here.

c_ice.say: 'P.S. The ice is good now.' I'll put it at the bottom, after 'Still Tuesdays'. They'll like that. I'm sure they read them.

c_time.say: 'The Mallards now keep time.' Yes. It sounds like a job. We've never had a job before. As a team.

c_here.say: 'Still here.' That's what I always say. But it's nice to hear somebody else say it.

done.say: Still Tuesdays. Still here. Thank you.
